study type: Prospective observational study with an accompanying animal model experiment
exposure: Maternal immunoglobulin A (IgA) in maternal milk
Domination by Enterobacteriaceae in the IgA-unbound fraction of the microbiota
cohort: The human cohort consisted of preterm infants whose fecal bacteria and IgA binding were analyzed.
finding: Maternal IgA in breast milk is a critical and necessary factor for the prevention of NEC in preterm neonates, as a decrease in IgA-bound bacteria and an increase in unbound Enterobacteriaceae are associated with NEC development.
followup_time: Up to the first month of life or until NEC onset
